title: RFL Simulator Conformance Declaration
description: A simulator's declaration for recursive conformance (spec/05 § Recursive simulator conformance). Test class 4 (end-to-end) accepts a high-fidelity simulator in place of physical hardware only if it is declared conformant: its outputs match a PHYSICALLY-conformant embodiment's outputs within the Class 2-loose ε on a reference fixture set. A simulator cannot bootstrap its own fidelity, so the declaration records its anchoring embodiment and reference fixtures. The ε-matching grade is `pending` until the ε-values are measured (the data-dependent item) and the simulator is run; invariant C10 (schemas/validate.py) enforces the no-self-bootstrap rule for a `conformant` claim.

anchoring_embodiment.description: The id of the PHYSICALLY-conformant embodiment whose outputs this simulator's fidelity is anchored to (spec/05: a simulator cannot bootstrap its own fidelity).

reference_fixtures.description: The (skill, embodiment) fixtures the simulator's outputs are matched against the anchoring embodiment on. Non-empty for a conformant claim.

tolerance_basis.description: The tolerance regime the output-matching uses. Class 2-loose (the per-skill ε-tolerance table) is the only basis for a contact-dynamics anchor.

conformance_status.description: pending = declared but not yet ε-matched (ε-values pending, or the simulator not yet run); conformant = matched the anchoring embodiment within ε on the fixtures; non_conformant = failed the match.

epsilon_match.description: The ε-match evidence (required by C10 for a `conformant` status): the worst per-quantity margin against the ε-table, and the date the match was run. Absent while `pending`.
